I ran out of tool calls before finishing, so there is no tar.gz yet. Nothing below has been compiled; the .NET SDK isn’t available here. Here’s where things stand.

Defect #3: the canvas showing “New message: …”
Enhanced navigation reuses DOM elements across pages. The board page ended with <p id="board-announcer">, and the canvas page ends with <p class="note">. Both are a <p> after the island, so Blazor turned one into the other. The board’s JavaScript had already written “New message: …” into that element, so the text carried over onto the canvas page. The slots page had the same flaw with slots-announcer.

The fix is written:

Shared announcer: there is now one #announcer region in MainLayout, marked data-permanent, which App.razor.js will clear on each enhancedload. The per-page announcer paragraphs are removed.
Stale clients: the board and slots clients no longer announce after they are disposed or once their feed is detached from the page.
Finished, not yet packaged
Server clock. The footer renders the server’s time, Unix milliseconds and UTC offset into a data-permanent <time id="server-clock"> (ServerClock.cs). The plan is for JavaScript to tick it from performance.now() and resync against a new /time JSON endpoint. That ticking and resync code isn’t written yet.
Character count. A 0 / 500 counter updates on every input or paste, in JavaScript, with no server round trip. After a successful post the island tells the JavaScript to recount. It turns red at the limit.
Canvas persistence (server and client written):
Server-minted UUIDv7 stroke ids and reset ids, kept strictly increasing by a new Uuid7.After.
The browser stores finished strokes in IndexedDB (chaos-canvas, capped at 10,000) and records the latest reset, deleting older strokes when one arrives.
On every snapshot it offers back a newer reset if it has one, then up to 500 missing strokes. Only strokes stamped before the server started and newer than the latest reset are offered, within the server’s free point budget.
The server validates offers and broadcasts a new merge update. An adopted reset bumps the epoch and re-sends the snapshot to everyone.
Latency page, server side:
A catalog of 37 public endpoints: this site, Cloudflare, Google, Apple, Microsoft, Mozilla, GitHub, Wikipedia, package registries, and 17 AWS DynamoDB /ping regions.
A compact result format, key=browser,server;….
HttpLatencyProbe: one warm-up request, then the best of 3, 6 in parallel, with a 30 s budget.
LatencyService: one run at a time, a 10 s global gap, a 5-minute per-client cooldown, keeps the last 50 runs, broadcasts a “running” state, and accepts offers like slots. No IP addresses are stored.
